NASB.1: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
NASB.2: 'Son of man, how is the wood of the vine [better] than any wood of a branch which is among the trees of the forest?
NASB.3: 'Can wood be taken from it to make anything, or can [men] take a peg from it on which to hang any vessel?
NASB.4: 'If it has been put into the fire for fuel, [and] the fire has consumed both of its ends and its middle part has been charred, is it [then] useful for anything?
NASB.5: 'Behold, while it is intact, it is not made into anything. How much less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it still be made into anything!
NASB.6: 'Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD, 'As the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem;
NASB.7: and I set My face against them. [Though] they have come out of the fire, yet the fire will consume them. Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I set My face against them.
NASB.8: 'Thus I will make the land desolate, because they have acted unfaithfully,'' declares the Lord GOD.

ESV.1: And the word of the LORD came to me:
ESV.2: “Son of man, how does the wood of the vine surpass any wood, the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?
ESV.3: Is wood taken from it to make anything? Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on it?
ESV.4: Behold, it is given to the fire for fuel. When the fire has consumed both ends of it, and the middle of it is charred, is it useful for anything?
ESV.5: Behold, when it was whole, it was used for nothing. How much less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it ever be used for anything!
ESV.6: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
ESV.7: And I will set my face against them. Though they escape from the fire, the fire shall yet consume them, and you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.
ESV.8: And I will make the land desolate, because they have acted faithlessly, declares the Lord GOD.”

NKJV.4: Instead, it is thrown into the fire for fuel; the fire devours both ends of it, and its middle is burned. Is it useful for any work?

NKJV.8: Thus I will make the land desolate, because they have persisted in unfaithfulness,’ says the Lord GOD.”

AMP.1: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
AMP.2: "Son of man, how is the wood of the grapevine (Israel) better than any wood of a branch which is among the trees of the forest?
AMP.3: Can wood be taken from it to make any object? Or can men take a peg from it on which to hang any vessel?

NLT.1: Then this message came to me from the LORD:
NLT.2: “Son of man, how does a grapevine compare to a tree? Is a vine’s wood as useful as the wood of a tree?
NLT.3: Can its wood be used for making things, like pegs to hang up pots and pans?
NLT.4: No, it can only be used for fuel, and even as fuel, it burns too quickly.
NLT.5: Vines are useless both before and after being put into the fire!
NLT.6: “And this is what the Sovereign LORD says: The people of Jerusalem are like grapevines growing among the trees of the forest. Since they are useless, I have thrown them on the fire to be burned.
NLT.7: And I will see to it that if they escape from one fire, they will fall into another. When I turn against them, you will know that I am the LORD.
NLT.8: And I will make the land desolate because my people have been unfaithful to me. I, the Sovereign LORD, have spoken!”

WEB.1: Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,
WEB.2: “Son of man, what is the vine tree more than any tree, the vine-branch which is among the trees of the forest?
WEB.3: Will wood be taken of it to make anything? Will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel on it?
WEB.4: Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire has devoured both its ends, and the middle of it is burned. Is it profitable for any work?
WEB.5: Behold, when it was whole, it was suitable for no work. How much less, when the fire has devoured it, and it is burned, will it yet be suitable for any work?”
WEB.6: Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh: “As the vine tree among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so will I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
WEB.7: I will set my face against them. They will go out from the fire, but the fire will devour them; and you will know that I am Yahweh, when I set my face against them.
WEB.8: I will make the land desolate, because they have committed a trespass,” says the Lord Yahweh.

CSB17.1: Then the word of the LORD came to me:
CSB17.2: “Son of man, how does the wood of the vine, <sup>ⓐ</sup> that branch among the trees of the forest, compare to any other wood?
CSB17.3: Can wood be taken from it to make something useful? Or can anyone make a peg from it to hang things on?
CSB17.4: In fact, it is put into the fire as fuel. <sup>ⓑ</sup> The fire devours both of its ends, and the middle is charred. Can it be useful for anything?
CSB17.5: Even when it was whole it could not be made into a useful object. How much less can it ever be made into anything useful when the fire has devoured it and it is charred!”
CSB17.6: Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says, “Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire as fuel, so I will give up the residents of Jerusalem.
CSB17.7: I will turn against them. <sup>ⓒ</sup> They may have escaped from the fire, but it will still consume them. <sup>ⓓ</sup> And you will know that I am the LORD when I turn against them.
CSB17.8: I will make the land desolate because they have acted unfaithfully.” This is the declaration of the Lord GOD.

MSG.2: "Son of man, how would you compare the wood of a vine with the branches of any tree you'd find in the forest?
MSG.3: Is vine wood ever used to make anything? Is it used to make pegs to hang things from?
MSG.4: "I don't think so. At best it's good for fuel. Look at it: a flimsy piece of vine, thrown in the fire and then rescued—the ends burned off and the middle charred. Now is it good for anything?
MSG.5: "Hardly. When it was whole it wasn't good for anything. Half-burned is no improvement. What's it good for?
MSG.6: "So here's the Message of God, the Master: Like the wood of the vine I selected from among the trees of the forest and used as fuel for the fire, just so I'll treat those who live in Jerusalem.
MSG.7: I am dead set against them. Even though at one time they got out of the fire charred, the fire's going to burn them up. When I take my stand against them, you'll realize that I am God.
MSG.8: I'll turn this country into a wilderness because they've been faithless." Decree of God, the Master.

NET.1: The word of the LORD came to me:
NET.2: “Son of man, of all the woody branches among the trees of the forest, what happens to the wood of the vine?
NET.3: Can wood be taken from it to make anything useful? Or can anyone make a peg from it to hang things on?
NET.4: No! It is thrown in the fire for fuel; when the fire has burned up both ends of it and it is charred in the middle, will it be useful for anything?
NET.5: Indeed! If it was not made into anything useful when it was whole, how much less can it be made into anything when the fire has burned it up and it is charred?
NET.6: “Therefore, this is what the sovereign LORD says: Like the wood of the vine is among the trees of the forest which I have provided as fuel for the fire — so I will provide the residents of Jerusalem as fuel.
NET.7: I will set my face against them — although they have escaped from the fire, the fire will still consume them! Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.
NET.8: I will make the land desolate because they have acted unfaithfully, declares the sovereign LORD.”

NIV.2: “Son of man, how is the wood of a vine better than that of a branch on any of the trees in the forest?

NIV.8: I will make the land desolate because they have been unfaithful, declares the Sovereign Lord.”
